exchanges.question: What drove the improvement in the current accident year loss ratio vs 2Q25, unlike other commercial insurers (non-cat property, mix, loss picks)? Follow-up: will the ceding commission rate on reinsurance keep rising after the renewals?
exchanges.answer: Allibhai: losses came in below expectations as in the last few quarters; nothing out of the ordinary, normal variability and mix across a dozen statutory lines; reserves are as conservative as ever in company history. Petrucelli: treaties renewed June 1st so only one month of the new treaty is in Q2; could see a slight uptick in the commission ratio, possibly offset by AI-driven operating efficiency; the Q2 expense ratio should be a good measure going forward.

exchanges.question: With E&S casualty softening (GWP up 3% vs up 4% in Q1), how much are ROEs compressing in the line assuming loss trend views (high single to low double digits) are unchanged? Follow-up: how is Kinsale thinking about broker commissions in a softer market, given brokers may be placing more with admitted carriers?
exchanges.answer: Kinsale manages everything to a 20% ROE or greater; most product lines are probably running ahead of that; ROE was 24.4% for the quarter; balancing profit and growth. On commissions: acknowledged normal tension between wholesalers, retailers and buyers, worse in a soft market; argued Kinsale offers the best service (quote ratio, response time) and broadest risk appetite, and continues to grow ex the Commercial Property Division, which is going through a unique correction. Did not indicate any change to commission levels.

exchanges.question: Is 2Q the trough for commercial property, with larger players pulling out; could pricing become less negative in 2027 or could Kinsale return to large shared placements? Follow-up: what is driving the 3.7% growth ex large account property, is business returning to the admitted market, and what would make growth inflect?
exchanges.answer: No telling where property goes in 2027; still pressure from London MGAs and traditional markets on shared and layered deals, larger limits, stretch primaries; Kinsale will price to return thresholds and accept shrinking in that division. London competition is creeping into other long-tail liability occurrence lines, depressing Construction pricing, with more competition in general casualty; Kinsale will lean into pockets of opportunity. There is some flow to the admitted market but it is not pervasive.

exchanges.question: How much of the increase in inbound accounts cited in the press release comes from broker engagement vs more competitive pricing? Follow-ups: view on social inflation and casualty loss trends; and was the accident year loss ratio benefit entirely short-tail property?
exchanges.answer: Winston: a bit of both; the idle broker initiative is re-engaging lapsed brokers; hit ratios roughly the same for renewal and new business, so submission growth means more binds. Kehoe: language added to explain confidence in the model; Commercial Property crisis is over and rates are coming down dramatically, but the underlying business model works. Allibhai: casualty loss cost trend probably mid-single digits, varying by line; little social inflation seen given smaller accounts and lower limits; short-tail lines performing especially well, across the board. Kehoe: being more conservative, slowing IBNR release in longer-tail occurrence business and letting it flow faster in short-tail lines.

exchanges.question: Granularity on property pricing in Q2 vs Q1 and when it might reach equilibrium? Follow-ups: with mix shifting from more-profitable property to casualty, should the current accident year loss ratio drift up; and how will buyback pacing evolve?
exchanges.answer: Kehoe: equilibrium will come eventually since cats do happen, but no insight into when; other property divisions see growth. Winston: Agribusiness Property and small business property are more stable; Inland Marine (five product buckets) seeing a little more competition; people are starting to get to the floor of property pricing, still pressure from London. Allibhai: hard to say, loss ratio could drift up over time; losses below expectations; Kehoe: IBNR conservatism is a positive indicator. Buyback: will continue to lean in; first $100 million authorization exhausted, then $250 million with about $80 million left, plus the new $250 million; principal capital allocation strategy while growth is limited, growth remains first priority when it accelerates.

exchanges.question: How has product expansion contributed to growth over the past year, and what is the potential growth uplift from new products going forward?
exchanges.answer: New products are rolled out at a crawl, walk, run pace, never jumping in feet first. They are creating growth, driving submissions and new premium, but it will be slow growth; will ramp up as the market turns. No quantification given.
